 BNPB proposes weather modification, minimize Sumatra floods risks
 November 17, 2026 11:13 GMT+700 
 BNPB Head Kristomei Sianturi in a press statement after attending a hydrometeorological disaster preparedness coordination meeting for the North Sumatra and Aceh region, at Soewondo Air Base in Medan, Monday (November 16, 2026). ANTARA/Muhammad Said 
 Medan, North Sumatra (ANTARA) - The Head of the National Agency for Disaster Countermeasures (BNPB), Lieutenant General Kristomei Sianturi, said the agency has proposed weather modification operations to reduce rain intensity and prevent further flooding in three provinces in Sumatra.
"We have heard requests from regional leaders, requesting weather modification operations," he said after attending a coordination meeting on hydrometeorological disaster preparedness for the North Sumatra and Aceh regions at Soewondo Air Base in Medan on Monday (Nov 16).
The BNPB had received several letters of request from local governments requesting weather modification operations as an effort to reduce rainfall intensity.
The first request came from Aceh Provincial administration to reduce the intensity of rainfall in the region.
"We have also offered the Governor of North Sumatra the similar measure to help reduce rainfall intensity in the province," Sianturi said.
He explained the weather modification operation is not intended to eliminate rainfall entirely, but rather to regulate its intensity in specific areas to mitigate the risk of flooding.
In addition to updating disaster risk assessments, regional governments should identify disaster mitigation priorities and strengthen their preparedness for hydrometeorological disasters.
Earlier, President Prabowo Subianto has instructed the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), the BNPB, and other relevant agencies to conduct weather modification operations in several disaster-affected areas in Sumatra to prevent further disasters.
Home Affairs Minister Tito Karnavian, who heads the Sumatra Post-Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Acceleration Task Force, explained that 41 subsequent disasters occurred in several affected areas of Aceh, North Sumatra, and West Sumatra between April 2026 and November 2026.
"Our priority is prevention. Through weather modification operations, we aim to minimize rainfall in the disaster-affected areas," Tito said, adding that if rainfall does occur, the operation hopefully can minimize its impact.
The government would ensure that facilities, equipment, tents, food supplies, and other essential assistance are ready for affected communities.
